diagnostics.fix: The kernel could not establish compatible DERIVED decimal scales here. Numeric == / != carries a known SIGNED scale or unknown plus an independent multiplicative-constant capability: when known scales differ, only a capable SMALLER-scale side may be padded; an unknown scale rejects. ORDERING (< <= > >=) is exempt. TWO contexts trigger this code: (1) a COMPUTED FIELD whose declared scale is incompatible with its expression (e.g. a field re-scaled to 2 places while the Sum-computed field stays scale 0) — re-scale the computed field or explicitly round the expression, doing both edits in ONE `apply` so the terminal gate sees a consistent model; expect a SECOND rejection to surface if the operation also reads its own computed field, because this scale comparison is decided ahead of that refusal; (2) numeric == / != with incompatible derived scales — round one side to a known compatible scale, or accept it with allowDifferingDecimals:true on the rule spec (the kernel's one suppressible warning — it prepends @SuppressWarning(MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES)).
diagnostics.explain: MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES ("the fractional digits of lhs and rhs are different") fires when numeric == / != cannot reconcile the operands' derived signed-scale/capability summaries, OR when a computed field is incompatible with its expression. It is not specific to any one operator (Sum, Equal, …); the scale-coupling is the constraint, so the corrective is context-dependent.

diagnostics.fix: A repeatable group is referenced from a rule that does not iterate over it — the fix is operator-dependent. For an AGGREGATE, flatten the repetitions with the `*` wildcard: Sum(Lines*/Amount), NumberOfFilledFields(Lines*/Sku), NumberOfFilledGroups(Lines*). For a PER-REPETITION predicate (RepetitionNotUnique / CurrentRepetition), make the rule iterate by putting its group at the PARENT of the repeated group with the error field inside it — via the CLI, `rule check --group <parentGroup> --field <parentGroup>/<repeatedGroup>/<field>` (e.g. --group /Order --field /Order/Items/Sku for RepetitionNotUnique(Items/Sku)).
diagnostics.explain: MVK_NO_WILDCARD fires when a repeatable group is referenced from a non-iterating scope: the kernel expected either a flattening `*` (aggregates) or a rule that iterates over that group (per-repetition predicates). The required form depends on the operator, so this code is not specific to any single one.

Rule with path '/Probe/CheckRule': The maximum number of fractional digits of the left-hand side (0) and of the right-hand side (1) are different. [MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES]
diagnostics.fix: The kernel could not establish compatible DERIVED decimal scales here. Numeric == / != carries a known SIGNED scale or unknown plus an independent multiplicative-constant capability: when known scales differ, only a capable SMALLER-scale side may be padded; an unknown scale rejects. ORDERING (< <= > >=) is exempt. TWO contexts trigger this code: (1) a COMPUTED FIELD whose declared scale is incompatible with its expression (e.g. a field re-scaled to 2 places while the Sum-computed field stays scale 0) — re-scale the computed field or explicitly round the expression, doing both edits in ONE `apply` so the terminal gate sees a consistent model; expect a SECOND rejection to surface if the operation also reads its own computed field, because this scale comparison is decided ahead of that refusal; (2) numeric == / != with incompatible derived scales — round one side to a known compatible scale, or accept it with allowDifferingDecimals:true on the rule spec (the kernel's one suppressible warning — it prepends @SuppressWarning(MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES)).
diagnostics.explain: MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES ("the fractional digits of lhs and rhs are different") fires when numeric == / != cannot reconcile the operands' derived signed-scale/capability summaries, OR when a computed field is incompatible with its expression. It is not specific to any one operator (Sum, Equal, …); the scale-coupling is the constraint, so the corrective is context-dependent.

Rule with path '/Probe/CheckRule': Missing specification of an asterisk for 'Rows' in '/Probe/Rows/RowVal'. [MVK_NO_WILDCARD]
diagnostics.fix: A repeatable group is referenced from a rule that does not iterate over it — the fix is operator-dependent. For an AGGREGATE, flatten the repetitions with the `*` wildcard: Sum(Lines*/Amount), NumberOfFilledFields(Lines*/Sku), NumberOfFilledGroups(Lines*). For a PER-REPETITION predicate (RepetitionNotUnique / CurrentRepetition), make the rule iterate by putting its group at the PARENT of the repeated group with the error field inside it — via the CLI, `rule check --group <parentGroup> --field <parentGroup>/<repeatedGroup>/<field>` (e.g. --group /Order --field /Order/Items/Sku for RepetitionNotUnique(Items/Sku)).
diagnostics.explain: MVK_NO_WILDCARD fires when a repeatable group is referenced from a non-iterating scope: the kernel expected either a flattening `*` (aggregates) or a rule that iterates over that group (per-repetition predicates). The required form depends on the operator, so this code is not specific to any single one.
